originals.citation: Kakiuchi, C., Ishiwata, M., et al. (2004). Association of the XBP1-116C/G polymorphism with schizophrenia in the Japanese population. Psychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences.

Chen, W., Duan, S., et al. (2004). A case-control study provides evidence of association for a functional polymorphism -197C/G in XBP1 to schizophrenia and suggests a sex-dependent effect. Biochem Biophys Res Commun.

quote: A functional promoter polymorphism (-116C/G) of the X-box binding protein 1 gene (XBP1) gene was reported to be associated with schizophrenia in Asian subjects. In a replication attempt, three European case-control samples ... were genotyped
notes: Full text paywalled. 'Asian subjects' = the Japanese (Kakiuchi 2004) and Chinese (Chen 2004; same SNP under -197 numbering, I believe) schizophrenia reports; meta-analysis total 3,612 minus 2,182 new = 1,430 prior subjects, consistent with both. Chen2004 inclusion less certain. Kakiuchi2003/Hou2004/Cichon2004 are bipolar studies (background). DOI for Chen2004 not verified.
